```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Use quarto render to generate a static site in /docs
# Set github pages to deploy from main branch, /docs

# Insure packages are installed by checking required packages against installed packages
reqd_pkgs <- c("flextable",
               "sf",
               "tidyverse",
               "mapgl",
               "htmltools",
               "officer",
               "socratadata",
               "forcats")

install.packages(
  setdiff(
    reqd_pkgs,
    rownames(installed.packages())
  ),
  repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
)

lapply(reqd_pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE) |> 
  invisible()

# If needed, ensure that the Quarto render and RStudio read the same environment vars
readRenviron(".Renviron")

set_flextable_defaults(
  font.family  = "Authentic Sans",
  font.size    = 10,        # ~13px (flextable uses points)
  border.color = "#0b0b0b",
  background.color = "transparent",
  padding.top    = 8,
  padding.bottom = 4,
  padding.left   = 0,
  padding.right  = 16
)

# Wraps a data frame in a CIL-styled flextable ready to embed in the page.
# Columns size to their content by default. `widths` overrides that: one value
# per column, or named values setting just those columns. `max_width` caps the
# fitted widths, never the ones `widths` names. `full_height = TRUE` drops the
# 400px cap so the whole table renders inline without a vertical scrollbar.
# `unit = "%"` reads `widths` as shares of a full-width table instead of
# absolute sizes, which is how two tables are given matching columns.
# Usage: data |> cil_table(widths = c("Purpose of Funds" = 4))
#        data |> cil_table(widths = c(39, 61), unit = "%")
cil_table <- function(data, widths = NULL, heights = NULL,
                      max_width = NULL, unit = "in", full_width = TRUE,
                      full_height = FALSE) {
  ft <- flextable(data)
  pct <- identical(unit, "%")
  # Percentages never reach flextable, so they don't take the fitted path below.
  fitted <- !pct && !(is.null(widths) && is.null(max_width))

  if (pct) {
    if (is.null(widths)) {
      stop("`unit = \"%\"` sets column shares, so it needs `widths`.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(max_width)) {
      stop("`max_width` caps fitted widths in absolute units; `unit = \"%\"` ",
           "sets shares outright. Use one or the other.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!full_width) {
      stop("Percentage widths are shares of a full-width table. Leave ",
           "`full_width = TRUE`.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (!is.null(heights)) {
      # `unit` covers heights too, and a row can't be a percentage of anything.
      stop("`heights` needs an absolute unit, which `unit = \"%\"` overrides. ",
           "Set column shares and row heights in separate calls.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (length(widths) != ncol(data)) {
      # Named subsets work for absolute widths because dim_pretty() supplies a
      # baseline for the columns left out. Shares have no such baseline.
      stop("`widths` has ", length(widths), " value(s) but `data` has ",
           ncol(data), " column(s). Percentage widths need one per column.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }

  if (fitted && full_width) {
    stop("`full_width` stretches columns to the container; `widths`/`max_width` ",
         "pin them. Use one or the other.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!fitted) {
    # Browser-side content fitting, like Excel's Autofit. width = 0 leaves the
    # table unconstrained; width = 1 would stretch it to 100% regardless of text.
    ft <- set_table_properties(ft, if (full_width) 1 else 0, layout = "autofit")
  } else {
    # Fitted widths are the baseline, capped by max_width, then overridden by
    # anything `widths` names. "autofit" discards widths, so this must be fixed.
    fit <- unlist(dim_pretty(ft)$widths)
    if (!is.null(max_width)) fit <- pmin(fit, max_width)
    if (is.null(widths)) {
      widths <- fit
    } else if (!is.null(names(widths)) && all(nzchar(names(widths)))) {
      unknown <- setdiff(names(widths), names(data))
      if (length(unknown)) {
        stop("`widths` names no such column: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "),
             call. = FALSE)
      }
      fit[match(names(widths), names(data))] <- widths
      widths <- fit
    } else if (length(widths) != ncol(data)) {
      # Otherwise they land on the first columns, misaligning every one.
      stop("`widths` has ", length(widths), " value(s) but `data` has ",
           ncol(data), " column(s). Give one width per column, or name them.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
    ft <- set_table_properties(ft, layout = "fixed")
    ft <- width(ft, j = seq_along(widths), width = widths, unit = unit)
  }

  if (!is.null(heights)) {
    # Heights are only emitted under the "exact" rule; "auto" ignores them.
    ft <- height(ft, height = heights, part = "body", unit = unit)
    ft <- hrule(ft, rule = "exact", part = "body")
  }

  # flextable's width() speaks only in/cm/mm, and autofit emits no column widths
  # at all, so shares are carried by markup instead: a <colgroup> the browser
  # obeys once .scroll-output--pct switches the table to `table-layout: fixed`.
  # Empty otherwise, leaving the sub() below a no-op.
  colgroup <- if (pct) {
    paste0("<colgroup>",
           paste0(sprintf('<col style="width:%s%%;">', widths), collapse = ""),
           "</colgroup>")
  } else ""

  ft |>
    border_remove() |>
    bold(bold = TRUE, part = "header") |>
    hline(border = fp_border(color = "#0b0b0b", width = 1.5),  part = "header") |>
    hline(border = fp_border(color = "#969696", width = 0.75), part = "body") |>
    # hline() mirrors each rule onto the next row's top edge as well as the
    # current row's bottom. Under the `border-collapse: separate` these tables
    # need for sticky headers, the two edges stack instead of merging, so every
    # interior rule renders at double weight -- only the final one, with no row
    # below it, looks right. Clearing the tops leaves a single 0.75pt line.
    border(border.top = fp_border(width = 0), part = "body") |>
    padding(
      padding.top = 0, padding.bottom = 4,
      padding.left = 0, padding.right = 16,
      part = "header"
    ) |>
    # Both steps are needed to keep the table out of a shadow DOM, which no page
    # CSS can reach: ft.shadow drops the static host, and the rename hides the
    # wrapper from tabwid.js, which shadow-roots every .tabwid on DOMContentLoaded.
    htmltools_value(ft.shadow = FALSE) |>
    as.character() |>
    sub(pattern = 'class="tabwid"', replacement = 'class="cil-tabwid"', fixed = TRUE) |>
    sub(pattern = "(<table[^>]*>)", replacement = paste0("\\1", colgroup)) |>
    HTML() |>
    div(class = paste(
      c("scroll-output",
        if (fitted) "scroll-output--fit",
        if (pct) "scroll-output--pct",
        if (full_height) "scroll-output--full"),
      collapse = " "
    ))
}

```
# Hazard Categories

The Queens Resource Map will display ranked hazard-related preparedness and recovery resources and messaging at the Community District Tabulation Area (CDTA) level. 

Our hazard categorization is based on New York City's 2024 Jurisdictional Risk Assessment[^1] report. The 2024 report uses the Pennsylvania Public Health Risk Assessment Tool (PHRAT) model in order to develop a "Planning Priority Score" used to suggest where New York City should focus its resources and planning efforts. The ten categories defined by the 2024 JRA report and their rank are: 

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~Rank, ~`JRA Hazard`,
    "1", "Flooding",
    "2", "Hazardous Materials Release",
    "3", "Pandemic",
    "4", "Infectious Disease Outbreak",
    "5", "Coastal Storm",
    "6", "Mass Casualty Event",
    "7", "Chemical Threats",
    "8", "Temperature Extremes",
    "9", "Utility Interruption",
    "10", "Cyberattack"
  ),
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%",
  full_height = TRUE
)
```

Our intended user is a New Yorker concerned about an imminent threat, rather than a municpal agency or staffer. To support this use case, we've modified the hazard categorization accordingly:

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~`Queens Map Hazard`, ~Notes,
    "Heavy Rain", "Added to capture non-coastal stormwater flooding",
    "Coastal Storm", "",
    "Extreme Heat", "Broken out from Temperature Extremes",
    "Extreme Cold", "Broken out from Temperature Extremes",
    "Hazmat / Chemical", "Combines Hazardous Materials Release and Chemical Threats",
    "Mass Casualty Event / Active Shooter", "Extends Mass Casualty Event",
    "Infectious Disease", "Combines Pandemic and Infectious Disease Outbreak",
    "Blackout & Cyberattack (EMP)", "Combines Utility Interruption and Cyberattack"
  ),
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%"
)
```


[^1]: [Jurisdictional Risk Assessment 2024, New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/498014fede58495dae447d97c6bf1611)

# Hazard Ranking

## Data Sources
Hazard ranking among Queens CDTAs requires data sources that can be used to differentiate the relative risks between districts. These data are not available for all hazards:

```{r}
#| echo: false

cil_table(
  tribble(
    ~`Queens Map Hazard`, ~`Data Source`,
    "Heavy Rain", "Stormwater Flood Maps",
    "Coastal Storm", "Current-day Storm Surge FVI",
    "Extreme Heat", "Heat Vulnerability Index",
    "Extreme Cold", "None available",
    "Hazmat / Chemical", "Chemically Intensive Small Businesses\nHazardous Waste Material Storage",
    "Mass Casualty Event / Active Shooter", "None available",
    "Infectious Disease", "Pandemic Influenza Vulnerability Index",
    "Blackout & Cyberattack (EMP)", "None available"
  ),
  full_height = TRUE,
  widths = c(39, 61),
  unit = "%"
)
```

In the absence of available information at the Community District level, extreme cold, mass casualty events / active shooter incidents, and blackout & cyberattack cannot be ranked.

In order to identify a suitable ranking methodology for the remaining hazards, a discussion of the disparate data is warranted. 

```{r}
#| cache: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Fetch data sources

cdta <- read_sf("https://services5.arcgis.com/GfwWNkhOj9bNBqoJ/arcgis/rest/services/NYC_Community_District_Tabulation_Areas_2020/FeatureServer/0/query?where=CDTAType=0&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson") |> 
  mutate(cdtaCode = paste0(
    BoroCode,
    str_sub(CDTA2020, -2)
  ))

stormwater_limited <- read_sf("https://github.com/BetaNYC/q-map/releases/download/data-v4/stormwater_limited_1_77.geojson") |> st_make_valid()

stormwater_moderate <- read_sf("https://github.com/BetaNYC/q-map/releases/download/data-v4/stormwater_moderate_2_13.geojson") |> 
  st_make_valid()

ss_cur_fvi <- soc_read(
  "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Environment/New-York-City-s-Flood-Vulnerability-Index/mrjc-v9pm.json",
  query = soc_query(
    select = "the_geom, GEOID, ss_cur"
  ),
  include_synthetic_cols = FALSE
)

hvi <- read_sf("https://services1.arcgis.com/8cuieNI8NbqQZQVJ/arcgis/rest/services/HVI_by_CDTA_CRAD_2024/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

chem_small_biz <- read_sf("https://services3.arcgis.com/A6Zjpzrub8ESZ3c7/arcgis/rest/services/Chemically%20Intensive%20Small%20Businesses_2/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

hazmat_storage <- read_sf("https://services6.arcgis.com/yG5s3afENB5iO9fj/arcgis/rest/services/EPA_RCA_Fuel_Oil_Storage/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

pivi <- read_sf("https://services1.arcgis.com/8cuieNI8NbqQZQVJ/arcgis/rest/services/Pandemic_Influenza_Vulnerability_Index/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=pgeojson")

# Aggregate where needed

## Stormwater -> CDTA
stormwater_all <- st_union(
  st_union(stormwater_limited),
  st_union(stormwater_moderate)
) |> 
  st_transform(4326) |> 
  st_make_valid()

stormwater_pct <- cdta |> 
  mutate(cdta_area = st_area(geometry)) |> 
  st_intersection(stormwater_all) |> 
  transmute(CDTA2020,
            stormwater_pct = as.numeric(st_area(geometry) / cdta_area) * 100) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(stormwater_pct) |> 
  mutate(stormwater_pct = replace_na(stormwater_pct, 0))

## Tract-level FVI -> CDTA
# Assign max FVI to CD
ss_cur_fvi_cd <- ss_cur_fvi |> 
  st_join(cdta |> select(CDTA2020),
          largest = TRUE)

ss_cur_fvi_cd <- ss_cur_fvi_cd |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(CDTA2020) |> 
  summarize(max_ss_cur_fvi = max(ss_cur, na.rm = T))
 
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(ss_cur_fvi_cd)

# Hazmat storage
cdta$hazmat_count <- lengths(st_intersects(cdta, hazmat_storage))

# Join remainder

## HVI
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(hvi |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(CommDist, HVI),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == CommDist))

## Chemically Intensive Small Business count
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(chem_small_biz |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(BoroCD, top_3) |> 
              mutate(BoroCD = as.character(BoroCD)) |> 
              rename(chem_count = "top_3"),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == BoroCD))

## PIVI
cdta <- cdta |> 
  left_join(pivi |> 
              st_drop_geometry() |> 
              select(COMMDIST, PIVI),
            by = join_by(cdtaCode == COMMDIST))

cdta <- cdta |> 
  select(BoroCode,CDTA2020, cdtaCode, CDTAName,
         stormwater_pct, max_ss_cur_fvi, hazmat_count, HVI, chem_count, PIVI) |> 
  relocate(geometry, .after = last_col()) |> 
  mutate(max_ss_cur_fvi = as.integer(max_ss_cur_fvi))
```

## Heavy Rain

The impact of heavy rain on a given Community District is taken as the percent area that experiences stormwater flooding of any kind (i.e. greater than 4 inches of flooding without sea level rise under a limited- or moderate-intensity rainfall event). Citywide, this percentage ranges from `r round(min(cdta$stormwater_pct),2)`% to `r round(max(cdta$stormwater_pct),2)`%. In Queens, the percentage ranges from `r round(min(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$stormwater_pct),2)`% to `r round(max(cdta[cdta$BoroCode==4,]$stormwater_pct),2)`%. All 59 Community Districts experience some stormwater flooding.

```{r}
ggplot(cdta) + 
  geom_col(aes(x = fct_reorder(CDTA2020, stormwater_pct), 
               y = stormwater_pct,
               fill = BoroCode == 4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "#ea4943") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#3258a3", `FALSE` = "#cedef0"),
                    guide = "none") +
  theme(
    panel.background   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#ebebeb"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5)
    )+
  labs(title = "Stormwater Flood Extent in CDTAs", x = "CDTA", y = "Stormwater Flood Extent [%]") +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = median(cdta$stormwater_pct),
           label = "Citywide median", colour = "#ea4943",
           hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3)
```

Computing percentile rank in this case is straightforward:

```{r}
cdta <- cdta |> 
  mutate(stormwater_pctrank = 100 * ecdf(cdta$stormwater_pct)(cdta$stormwater_pct))

cil_table(cdta |> 
            st_drop_geometry() |> 
            filter(BoroCode == 4) |>
            select(CDTAName, stormwater_pctrank) |>
            mutate(stormwater_pctrank = round(stormwater_pctrank, 2)) |> 
            rename(
              "CDTA Name" = "CDTAName",
              "Stormwater Extent Percentile (Citywide)" = "stormwater_pctrank"
            ),
          full_height = TRUE) 
```
